editions.label: Wednesday, 25 November 2026
editions.note: Morning edition. Times are Sydney local unless noted. Reported plans, beta rollouts and unreleased features are labelled separately from available products.

stories.title: Western Sydney's young adults say investment is not easing everyday pressures
stories.summary: A new Western Sydney Leadership Dialogue survey finds 70% of respondents struggling with living costs, while around half identify housing affordability and job security as problems. Its author says major infrastructure spending has not translated into tangible short-term improvements for young people.
stories.detail: Published this morning, the survey covers 160 people aged 18 to 29 who live, work or study in the region, so it is a useful snapshot rather than a census of Western Sydney. A quarter also identify negative safety stereotypes as a barrier, adding a reputational burden to the financial squeeze.

stories.title: Mental health report finds longer emergency waits and more acute NSW cases
stories.summary: The AMA's new national hospital report card says one in ten mental health patients waits almost 24 hours in emergency before admission, with more than half of those ultimately admitted waiting over seven hours. In NSW, the share of presentations classified as an emergency rose from 11% to 20% over the past decade.
stories.detail: The report puts national capacity at 27 specialised public mental health beds per 100,000 people. Doctors are calling for earlier intervention, a stronger workforce and better coordination across services, with a new federal-state mental health agreement currently being negotiated.

stories.title: EU browser dispute escalates as Google backs Mozilla's complaint
stories.summary: Google's Chrome developer team has backed Mozilla's criticism of Apple's EU browser rules, while the European Commission says it is discussing the restrictions with Apple. The complaint is that developers cannot move existing iPhone users to an independent browser engine without making them install a separate app.
stories.detail: MacRumors published the Google development at 1 pm PST on 24 November, which is 8 am today in Sydney. Apple argues its approval conditions protect security and privacy; its documentation still restricts these alternative-engine entitlements to EU distribution, so this is regulatory pressure, not a new browser capability released for Australian iPhones.
stories.published: 25 November, 8:00 am AEDT (24 November, 1:00 pm PST)

stories.title: Report: Tesla and SpaceX negotiators target a possible year-end agreement
stories.summary: The Financial Times has identified five directors overseeing Tesla-SpaceX merger negotiations, with talks reportedly working towards a possible 31 December deadline. Electrek's account stresses that an agreement is not close, despite the target, and that shareholder approval and regulatory scrutiny would still lie ahead.
stories.detail: This is a potentially major change to Tesla's corporate structure, not routine share-price news or a completed deal. There is no confirmed change to Australian vehicle sales, servicing or your Model Y's features; any longer-term implications for investment priorities remain uncertain.
stories.published: 25 November, 1:43 am AEDT (24 November, 6:43 am PST)

stories.title: Robotaxi riders gain extra waiting time, but scheduled pickups are not live yet
stories.summary: Not a Tesla App reports that Robotaxi riders can now extend the pickup countdown in two-minute increments. Separately, code in app version 26.11.5 points to future scheduled pickups, including selecting and adjusting a pickup time.
stories.detail: The distinction matters: the waiting-time button has been observed working, whereas advance booking is still an unreleased feature found in code. This concerns Tesla's separate Robotaxi service, not a software upgrade for privately owned Model Ys, and the report does not establish Australian availability.

stories.title: Claude artifacts can now become personal Mac and Windows apps
stories.summary: Anthropic is rolling out an 'Install as app' beta across plans, giving artifacts their own window and icon, with optional notifications and connectors. They still require an online, signed-in Claude session, and requests count towards your existing usage limits rather than running as independent offline software.
stories.detail: Australia is a supported region, but rollout and organisation settings still apply; Enterprise owners must enable the feature. My suggested experiment: build a customer meeting-prep app using approved calendar and account data, initially keeping permissions restricted rather than granting full computer access.

stories.title: Claude connectors can deliver workflow expertise alongside their tools
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Skills over MCP in public beta, allowing connected services to supply reusable workflow instructions as well as actions. Tasks and Elicitation are generally available for supported individual plans, letting servers handle longer jobs and request input, while file uploads are still coming soon.
stories.detail: Skills are enabled by default for Pro, Max and Ultra, require Team admin approval and are not yet available to Enterprise; Tasks and Elicitation are rolling out to organisational plans. Australia is supported, with no special Australian exclusion stated; the practical opportunity is more consistent account research and follow-up workflows, provided the connector implements these capabilities.

stories.title: ABC plans to close Entertains and make a bigger move onto YouTube
stories.summary: The ABC's newly announced 2027 strategy will reduce its broadcast TV channels from four to three by discontinuing ABC Entertains. Managing director Hugh Marks also wants YouTube to become a primary distribution platform, with more channels and content created for audiences already watching there.
stories.detail: The channel closure is a planned change, not an overnight loss of service. The broadcaster expects its broader measures to redirect around $50 million a year into priorities including distinctive, live and local programming; separate news and current-affairs changes are due to be announced in early 2027.

stories.title: Nvidia's leadership reversal now faces a stronger congressional challenge
stories.summary: The new development after yesterday's reinstatement is bipartisan pressure for investigations, including Republican demands to explain the government's assurances to Nvidia's board. The scrutiny concerns suspected chip-export violations and the administration's involvement, rather than treating the CEO's return as the end of the matter.
stories.detail: ABC reports that Jensen Huang is scheduled for closed-door questioning by three House committees on 1 December and public Senate testimony on 3 December. The alleged export breaches remain allegations, and Nvidia's independent investigation is unfinished; this is a governance and AI-supply-chain story, not another recap of his return.

stories.title: Norway urges caution after Ukraine acknowledges a Gulf of Finland ship strike
stories.summary: Ukraine has acknowledged striking the Russian cargo vessel Sparta II, with Norway saying it has raised regional stability and international-law concerns with Kyiv. This is a separate operation from the Libya attack covered yesterday, and the latest development is the acknowledgement and allied response, not a claim that the strike happened overnight.
stories.detail: The attack occurred on Saturday; Finnish, Estonian and Russian vessels helped fight the resulting fire before the ship was towed back to Russian waters. Zelenskyy calls it a legitimate military target, while the episode adds to fears that the war could spread beyond its existing boundaries.

afternoon.note: New developments since this morning. Times are Sydney local unless noted.

stories.title: Auburn fire ant response expands after further detections
stories.summary: Further surveillance has found a more extensive fire ant presence in Auburn, prompting NSW to establish a taskforce and intensify treatment. Authorities say the ants are a multiple-queen form that is more complex to eradicate.
stories.detail: The government says this colony type has not previously been detected in NSW and tracing of high-risk materials is being expanded. If you spot a suspicious nest, leave it undisturbed, photograph it safely and report it to the Biosecurity Helpline on 1800 680 244.

stories.title: ICAC identifies entrenched misogynistic culture in NSW prisons
stories.summary: The NSW corruption watchdog's new report identifies a widespread culture of sexual harassment and misogyny in Corrective Services NSW, alongside poor complaint handling and fear of reprisals. It makes 10 recommendations to improve accountability and workplace processes.
stories.detail: ICAC made no corrupt conduct findings because the evidence did not meet the required threshold. Corrective Services NSW and the Department of Communities and Justice have accepted the recommendations.

stories.title: Jury finds Beau Lamarre-Condon guilty of murdering Sydney couple
stories.summary: A jury has found former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon guilty of murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies. The unanimous verdicts followed about two hours of deliberations.
stories.detail: Lamarre-Condon had pleaded not guilty and argued that he acted in self-defence. The verdict follows a lengthy NSW Supreme Court trial.

stories.title: Inflation rises to 4.9% ahead of the RBA's December meeting
stories.summary: Annual inflation rose to 4.9% in October from 4.3% in September, according to the ABS figures released today. The trimmed mean measure of underlying inflation also rose, from 3.6% to 3.8%.
stories.detail: Housing was the largest contributor to annual inflation. The figures will be among the information considered by the Reserve Bank at its next meeting, but they do not determine its interest-rate decision on their own.

stories.title: Australia and Solomon Islands sign security and cooperation treaty
stories.summary: Anthony Albanese and Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale have signed a wide-ranging treaty covering security and cooperation. Solomon Islands has committed to consult Australia on sensitive infrastructure and not allow a foreign military or security base on its territory.
stories.detail: Australia also plans support for Solomon Islands policing and education, and new pathways for Solomon Islanders to work in aged care and childcare. Wale declined to confirm reports about the future of his country's China security pact, citing a non-disclosure clause.

stories.title: Pensioners exempted in deal on private health rebate cuts
stories.summary: The federal government has agreed to exempt full and part pensioners from its proposed cuts to private health insurance rebates for over-65s. The concession secures Greens support for the legislation in the Senate.
stories.detail: The government expects to forgo about half of the original $3 billion in projected savings over four years, while saying its planned aged-care investment will continue. The changes still need to pass Parliament.

editions.label: Tuesday, 24 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Rumours, future targets and availability limits are labelled.

stories.title: NSW report exposes a major gap in support for children facing family violence
stories.summary: New ABC reporting examines more than 91,000 child-protection reports relating to domestic and family violence in NSW in 2025/26. The state's children's advocate says about 66,000 were assessed as involving risk of significant harm, but around 48,000 of those were closed because no caseworker capacity was available.
stories.detail: These are reports, not 91,000 individual children, since one child may be reported more than once. The advocate's report, tabled on Friday, makes nine recommendations including specialist youth services and better coordination; today's story highlights the scale of the response gap rather than announcing those reforms have been implemented.

stories.title: New rental analysis shows how Sydney's averages conceal much harsher outcomes
stories.summary: Fresh SGS Economics and Planning analysis places Sydney among Australia's least affordable rental markets and finds the squeeze extending beyond the lowest-income groups. In Sydney, median rent represents about 84% of a single pensioner's income, while a typical single person on benefits would need more than their entire income.
stories.detail: The index compares median rents with different household incomes, so these are modelled affordability measures, not what every household actually pays. Canberra is the strongest capital-city market on the average measure, but even there lower-income renters remain under pressure; this is distinct from yesterday's proposal about investing NSW rental bonds.

stories.title: Former bus managers convicted over safety failures before the Hunter crash
stories.summary: Rodney and Katie Parker, former Linq Buslines managers, have each been convicted and fined $7,000 after pleading guilty to heavy-vehicle safety offences. The prosecution concerns failures before the 2023 Hunter wedding-bus crash that killed ten people.
stories.detail: The court heard Katie Parker had been told about driver Brett Button's opioid use months before the crash but had not made further enquiries. These are new management-level convictions, separate from Button's existing prison sentence; the judge reduced the fines because of guilty pleas and limited ability to pay.

stories.title: Report: Product(RED) HomePod mini and AirPods Max versions could arrive next week
stories.summary: 9to5Mac, citing Bloomberg, reports that Apple plans Product(RED) versions of HomePod mini 2 and AirPods Max 2 around 1 December. The suggested finishes include red speaker mesh and silver headphones with a red Digital Crown.
stories.detail: This remains a report, not an Apple announcement, with Australian pricing and availability unconfirmed. Published at 11:28 am Pacific on Monday, it falls at 6:28 am Tuesday in Sydney, inside this edition's 24-hour window.
stories.published: 24 Nov, 6:28 am Sydney (23 Nov, 11:28 am PST)

stories.title: Tesla scales back the planned memory increase for its next vehicle computer
stories.summary: Not a Tesla App reports Musk has revised AI4.5's planned memory from 64GB to 48GB in total, still above AI4's 32GB, citing rising memory costs and bandwidth limits. The upgraded computer is targeted for production around mid-2027, rather than being available now.
stories.detail: The report also says Musk continues to position AI5 for Optimus while vehicles use AI4 and AI4.5. For your Model Y, this is a future hardware direction, not a software upgrade: Tesla has not announced a retrofit option or confirmed Australian vehicle availability.

stories.title: Musk gives a tentative late-2027 target for wider Tesla Starlink integration
stories.summary: Musk says he hopes Starlink can be integrated across Tesla's vehicle range towards the end of 2027, according to Not a Tesla App. The fresh development is a timeline for expansion beyond Cybercab, not confirmation that existing consumer vehicles have received satellite internet.
stories.detail: Satellite backup could eventually help connectivity where mobile coverage is weak, although that is a potential benefit, not a confirmed Australian service. There is no announced retrofit, price or eligibility for your Model Y, and this should not be confused with a change to today's Premium Connectivity subscription.

stories.title: Gemini's API can now inspect selected slides, cells and recording segments
stories.summary: Google has launched native file slicing across Gemini 4 models, alongside uploads for Office and OpenDocument files. Developers can upload a file once, then request particular pages, spreadsheet ranges or media segments, with tokens billed for the material inspected rather than automatically processing the whole file.
stories.detail: Suggested work experiment: skim an approved EBR deck's text, identify the relevant results slide, then inspect just that slide's chart and footnotes before drafting a meeting brief. This is an API capability, not a new button in the consumer Gemini app; Google lists Australia as supported for the Gemini API and AI Studio, while existing file limits and account requirements still apply.

stories.title: Nvidia reverses course and reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
stories.summary: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang with immediate effect, reversing the board's recent statement that he would not return. The company says the decision was unanimous and followed input from senior US officials, making this a substantial leadership change at the centre of the AI supply chain.
stories.detail: The board says it is satisfied about his ability to lead and sees no national-security risk in his return. Those are the board's conclusions, not a blanket resolution of every issue: ABC reports investigations into the company's conduct are continuing, so the reinstatement should not be read as closing the wider Nvidia story.

stories.title: Ukraine claims a Russian warship sinking in Libya, widening the conflict's reach
stories.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury and damaged a military-linked cargo ship near Benghazi on Sunday. The acknowledgement brings Ukraine's operations into the open in Libya, well beyond the usual Black Sea theatre.
stories.detail: Libyan officials described serious damage and reported wounded Libyan and Russian nationals; Russian officials made no immediate comment on the Ukrainian account. The UN mission has called for an independent investigation and warned against Libya becoming a battleground for foreign conflicts.

stories.title: Rescuers find survivors as the Dymer strike death toll reaches eleven
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials say a seven-year-old boy and a 79-year-old woman were pulled alive from the rubble after Sunday's Russian strike on an apartment building in Dymer, near Kyiv. By Monday, the reported death toll had reached eleven, with two people's fate still unknown.
stories.detail: Search work was repeatedly interrupted by further attack threats. Zelenskyy renewed calls for tighter sanctions and export controls on the foreign components used in Russian drones.

afternoon.note: New developments since this morning. Times are Sydney local unless noted.

stories.title: Labor and Greens agree stronger online safety bill
stories.summary: Labor has secured Greens support for its proposed digital duty of care, including a right for Australians to sue social media companies over harm and maximum penalties of up to 5 per cent of global revenue. The agreement moves the bill closer to passage after negotiations over how strongly to regulate platforms.
stories.detail: The proposal would require platforms to take reasonable steps to address specified online harms, and allow users aged 16 and over to switch to a feed of accounts they follow. The bill still needs to pass Parliament, so the new rights and penalties are not yet in force.

stories.title: Australia and Singapore expand essential supplies cooperation
stories.summary: Australia and Singapore have signed an agreement to support trade in more essential goods during disruptions, extending cooperation beyond fuel and gas to products including food, medicines and telecommunications equipment. The leaders announced it after meeting in Canberra today.
stories.detail: They also signed an agreement establishing a framework for moving captured carbon dioxide from Singapore to Australia for offshore geological storage. The agreements set out cooperation and a framework, rather than confirming that a carbon storage project is already operating.

editions.label: Monday, 23 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates, proposals and availability limits are labelled. Categories without noteworthy new stories are omitted.

stories.title: Fire-ant nest found in Auburn, outside the existing control zone
stories.summary: A red imported fire-ant nest has been treated in Auburn after a resident reported it over the weekend. Authorities say it sits more than six kilometres from September's Enfield detection and could be around a year old, making this a separate and concerning discovery.
stories.detail: Properties within 500 metres will be inspected, with monitoring across a two-kilometre radius and detection dogs to follow. For western and inner-west Sydney residents, the useful action is to report suspicious nests through the Biosecurity Helpline on 1800 680 244; the report does not identify an Epping outbreak.

stories.title: Tenants' Union wants rental-bond returns to fund stronger enforcement
stories.summary: The NSW Tenants' Union argues that better investment of the state's $2.3 billion rental-bond pool could generate up to $200 million a year to support rental enforcement. That is the union's estimate and funding proposal, not an adopted government policy or a guaranteed return.
stories.detail: The rental commissioner says bond-account funding already supports advocacy, NCAT and regulation, while complaints rose to 10,745 in 2025/26. For renters and landlords, the immediate point is the debate over enforcement resources, not a new bond payment, refund entitlement or change to tenancy rules.

stories.title: FSD v15 is reaching cars, with Reality View, but the rollout is narrow
stories.summary: The material change since yesterday's December-release promise is an actual rollout of FSD v15.0.1 in software 2026.38.6.11. Not a Tesla App reports that initial availability appears limited to redesigned Model Y vehicles in the US and Canada, rather than a broad release to every owner.
stories.detail: Release notes add the AI-generated Reality View, revised route and parking selection, and improved detection of potholes and other hazards. Tesla's claimed 25-fold improvement concerns its critical-intervention measure, not independently demonstrated crash reduction; Australian availability and eligibility for your Model Y are not confirmed, and Tesla's Australian guidance still requires active driver supervision.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App; Tesla Australia support

stories.title: Small-business websites will be exempt from the proposed digital duty of care
stories.summary: Communications Minister Anika Wells says low-risk small-business websites, such as those of cafés and bookkeepers, will be exempt from the proposed digital duty of care. The clarification follows business concerns about uncertainty over who would be covered.
stories.detail: The Greens are negotiating amendments, including individuals' ability to take tech companies to court, so the bill is not yet settled. For customer-engagement conversations, this is a scope clarification to watch, not a blanket exemption for every app, AI chatbot or service operated by a small company.

stories.title: COP31 ends without its main deal after countries reject the final draft
stories.summary: The climate summit has now ended without agreement on its main pact, moving beyond yesterday afternoon's disputed draft. Australia and Türkiye, the joint presidencies, confirmed they would not offer another version after countries rejected a text that omitted fossil fuels.
stories.detail: The EU called it too weak, while developing countries objected to inadequate clarity on adaptation finance. This is a significant failure to agree new action after talks ran 44 hours beyond their scheduled finish, but it does not cancel countries' obligations from previous UN climate agreements.

stories.title: Government proposes keeping the $25 PBS medicines freeze until 2030
stories.summary: Anthony Albanese announced this morning that the government will move to extend the $25 PBS medicines price freeze until 2030. He said legislation would be introduced to parliament today, making this a new cost-of-living proposal rather than a measure already passed.
stories.detail: Health Minister Mark Butler linked the extension to patients having to choose between medicines and other household expenses, and the Pharmacy Guild welcomed it. The next step is the bill and its passage through parliament; today's announcement alone does not establish that all of its terms are law.

stories.title: West Bank arson attacks draw a sharp condemnation from Eisenkot
stories.summary: Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles and homes in Palestinian villages early on Sunday local time, with twelve vehicles reportedly burned across at least five villages. ABC obtained residents' footage from Kafr Malik and spoke to a resident who described families rushing to extinguish the fires.
stories.detail: Gadi Eisenkot, the politician trying to form Israel's next government, described the attacks as Jewish terrorism and called for arrests and severe sanctions. This is a fresh violence-and-accountability story, separate from yesterday's coalition-talks invitation; the report does not establish that the perpetrators have been arrested.

stories.title: Timor-Leste claims Chinese and Russian interest in Greater Sunrise
stories.summary: Timor-Leste's petroleum minister says unnamed companies, including some from China and Russia, have approached the government about Greater Sunrise after Woodside's exit. These are claims of interest, not signed investment commitments or a confirmed rescue of the oil and gas project north of Darwin.
stories.detail: The unresolved commercial problem is Timor-Leste's insistence on processing gas domestically rather than using existing Darwin infrastructure. Analysts quoted by ABC question the economics and warn that accepting strategically motivated finance could compromise economic independence, making this relevant to Australia's near neighbourhood as well as energy policy.

stories.title: Lowy's new Asia index finds the US-China power gap narrowing
stories.summary: The Lowy Institute's 2026 Asia Power Index finds US influence has declined while China has gained ground, although Washington still ranks as the region's dominant power. It puts their military-capability gap at its narrowest recorded level and Australia sixth overall, down one place.
stories.detail: The authors attribute much of the narrowing to US policy choices and the diversion of resources towards the Middle East, rather than a sudden Chinese leap. Treat this as a research institute's comparative assessment, not proof of an inevitable change in regional leadership or a new government policy.

afternoon.note: New developments since this morning. Times are Sydney local unless noted.

stories.title: Opera House access changes prompt safety concerns
stories.summary: Some patrons and staff have raised concerns about Sydney Opera House's changed accessible drop-off, which now uses the Macquarie Street Gatehouse and buggies to reach the building. Visitors told ABC the transfer can be difficult for people with limited mobility.
stories.detail: The arts workers' union says two incidents caused injuries to staff and a patron. The Opera House says the change avoids a working loading dock and that two of its three enclosed buggies have wheelchair ramps.

stories.title: Minns rules out a state funeral for Fred Nile
stories.summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns says there will be no state funeral for former MP Fred Nile. Sydney MP Alex Greenwich withdrew his earlier call for a state service and apologised after criticism from the LGBTQ+ community.
stories.detail: Greenwich said Nile's later work with him on LGBTQ+ reforms did not erase the hurt caused by his earlier campaigns. Minns said state funerals were reserved for rare circumstances.

stories.title: Queensland news-style Instagram account discloses LNP link
stories.summary: An Instagram account called Queensland Breaking News added a disclosure that it was authorised by the Liberal National Party after ABC asked questions about it. The LNP confirmed it uses the page to share information about its government's work.
stories.detail: The account had been posting government announcements under a news-style name. Queensland requires authorisation of election material in the 12 months before a state election, so the disclosure is not currently a legal requirement.

editions.label: Sunday, 22 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates, release dates and availability limits are labelled.

stories.title: One Nation rules out a formal NSW coalition, but leaves a power-sharing door open
stories.summary: NSW One Nation leader Mike Newman has ruled out joining a formal coalition with the Liberals and Nationals, while leaving confidence and supply open. Speaking at a Windsor firearms forum on Saturday, he also promised to unwind post-Bondi gun reforms.
stories.detail: The distinction matters ahead of next year's state election: a party can support a minority government's survival without joining its cabinet. Liberal leader Kellie Sloane has likewise rejected a formal coalition while leaving confidence and supply possible; these are political positions, not an agreed deal.

stories.title: Castle Hill investigation: police arrest a second teenager
stories.summary: Since yesterday afternoon's briefing, police have arrested a second teenager over the Castle Towers stabbings. ABC's later update says a 16-year-old was arrested at Castle Hill Police Station shortly before 5 pm on Saturday.
stories.detail: That is an arrest, not a reported charge against the second teenager. It advances the investigation beyond the earlier appeal for another person; police have not described the incident as a random attack.

stories.title: Apple's English-language support forums have now disappeared
stories.summary: MacRumors reports that the Apple Support Community forums have been removed, with their address redirecting to Apple's main support page. This is the actual removal, rather than another reminder of the previously announced closure.
stories.detail: The report was published on Saturday at 8:47 am PST, or 3:47 am Sunday in Sydney, inside this briefing's 24-hour window. French and German forums remained open at publication; old English-language troubleshooting links may now take you to general support instead of the original discussion.
stories.published: 22 Nov, 3:47 am Sydney (21 Nov, 8:47 am PST)

stories.title: Musk targets December's holiday update for a wider FSD v15 release
stories.summary: Elon Musk says FSD v15 will reach a wide release next month with Tesla's holiday update, and has endorsed questions about pothole avoidance and home-garage parking. Not a Tesla App also reports his promise of substantially revised driving visualisations.
stories.detail: Treat December as an announced target, not proof that these features have reached your Model Y. An Australian v15 rollout date and eligibility for your particular hardware cannot be confirmed; Tesla's Australian support guidance says functionality varies by configuration, software and region, and FSD still requires active driver supervision.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App; Tesla Australia support

stories.title: Inkling 2 Mini offers a practical route to offline AI on a capable Mac
stories.summary: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini with downloadable weights and Tinker access, not just a research preview. The release is dated 20 November, with fresh coverage on Saturday; the official model card supports Apple silicon Macs with at least 32GB of memory and describes a roughly 20GB checkpoint.
stories.detail: The local-download route is relevant in Australia without relying on an Australian hosted-service launch. Suggested experiment: use a sanitised meeting transcript to draft actions and follow-ups offline, then compare it with your usual tool; that is my suggestion, not a reported customer deployment, and its instruction-following limitations mean outputs still need checking.

stories.title: Reports of FBI and US agriculture-system hacks raise fresh security concerns
stories.summary: ABC reports that US media have identified apparent attacks on the FBI's national crime database and a Department of Agriculture payment system. The FBI system connects law-enforcement agencies and supports warrant and background checks, making data integrity as important as service uptime.
stories.detail: Who was responsible, and whether the incidents are linked, remain unclear. Keep these reported intrusions separate from the recent technical outages: there is no established basis for treating every disruption as one coordinated attack.

stories.title: Junior basketball's AI-camera trial draws privacy objections
stories.summary: Basketball Australia's Hoops TV camera system has been trialled in the Illawarra, Darwin and northern Brisbane, with wider rollout planned. It records games and uses AI to produce footage and statistics accessible through players' and guardians' basketball accounts.
stories.detail: ABC reports privacy and monetisation concerns, alongside a petition exceeding 13,000 signatures; Basketball Australia argues the platform offers more controlled access than informal filming. For families, the immediate question is the trial's opt-out process and who can view recordings, rather than assuming a camera is only capturing professional matches.

stories.title: COP31 overruns as the EU warns it could accept no deal
stories.summary: Climate talks have moved well beyond Friday's deadline without resolving fossil-fuel and finance disputes. The EU's climate chief said on Saturday that a satisfactory agreement was preferable to a weak compromise, even if that meant no deal.
stories.detail: The new development is the prolonged deadlock and explicit prospect of failure, not another draft-text recap. Turkey's presidency met Australian, EU and Saudi officials to seek a breakthrough; no final agreement was established in the reporting checked for this edition.
stories.published: 22 Nov, 1:36 am Sydney (21 Nov, 2:36 pm UTC)

stories.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's Likud into government-formation talks
stories.summary: Israel's Gadi Eisenkot has invited Likud to coalition negotiations beginning Sunday local time, after October's election produced no clear majority. He has until next month to assemble a government, while divisions persist within his own broad anti-Netanyahu camp.
stories.detail: An invitation is not a coalition agreement: Eisenkot has previously rejected serving under Netanyahu, and Naftali Bennett remains opposed to joining Netanyahu or his bloc. Whether negotiators can bridge that leadership divide is the key next development.

stories.title: CHOICE seeks urgent checks after NZ recalls children's garden kits
stories.summary: CHOICE is urging scrutiny of coloured-sand children's kits sold in Australia after asbestos was found in Faber-Castell products in New Zealand. The affected NZ ranges include garden and terrarium kits, but contamination of Australian stock has not been established.
stories.detail: Faber-Castell says Australian products are independently sourced, have undergone routine testing and are being reviewed further. The ACCC told ABC it was making enquiries and had not received a voluntary Australian recall from the company, so a New Zealand recall must not be presented as an Australian one.

stories.title: An offline island station leaves less time for tsunami response
stories.summary: Newly obtained documents show Macquarie Island's inactive seismic station has lengthened estimated regional earthquake detection from eight to ten minutes. The station lost power after personnel withdrew over bird-flu concerns, reducing the response window for potential Southern Ocean tsunamis affecting Australia's south-east.
stories.detail: Geoscience Australia says alerts should still meet the required ten-minute timeframe and hopes to install solar power for automation early next year. This is a newly reported monitoring gap, not a report of a current tsunami threat.

afternoon.note: New developments since this morning. Times are Sydney local unless noted.

stories.title: Former NSW MP Fred Nile dies aged 92
stories.summary: Fred Nile, a prominent and divisive figure in NSW politics for more than four decades, has died aged 92. His family announced his death on Sunday, saying he died peacefully on Saturday.
stories.detail: The former Christian Democratic Party leader served in the Legislative Council until 2023. A vocal opponent of same-sex marriage and abortion, he also helped pass legislation expunging historic homosexual convictions and worked with political opponents on protecting First Nations cultural sites.

stories.title: New COP31 draft sets an electrification target but omits fossil fuels
stories.summary: A new proposed COP31 agreement would aim to raise electricity's share of final energy use to 35 per cent by 2035, but again contains no explicit mention of fossil fuels. Its release gives countries a fresh text to consider as the summit runs into a second day of overtime.
stories.detail: The proposed wording also includes a goal for carbon capture and storage, a technology backed by the oil industry and criticised by some countries. Delegates still need to agree to the text, so it remains a proposal rather than a final deal.

editions.label: Saturday, 21 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates and availability limits are labelled.

stories.title: Mark Speakman will leave NSW parliament at the next election
stories.summary: The former NSW opposition leader says he will not recontest Cronulla, becoming the eighth Liberal MP to announce a departure in recent months. His late-night parliamentary speech also urged the party to retain its own identity rather than follow One Nation.
stories.detail: This is a planned exit at the 2027 election, not an immediate resignation or a new leadership contest. Kellie Sloane remains opposition leader and says she tried to persuade him to stay, adding another candidate-selection task before the state campaign.

stories.title: Heavy western NSW rain brings relief, but shuts unsealed roads
stories.summary: Pastoralists around the Darling-Baaka are celebrating substantial rain before summer, with one station north of Louth recording 204 mm. Other properties reported markedly different totals, so this is significant local relief rather than evidence that dry conditions have ended across NSW.
stories.detail: The ABC reported on Friday that almost all unsealed roads in the far west were closed, with rapid rises in local waterways. If travelling in that region this weekend, check current council road reports before setting out; Friday's closures should not be treated as a live Saturday road-status list.

stories.title: Signal blocks iPhone screenshots to keep AI out of chats
stories.summary: Signal's new protection blocks screenshots on iOS 27 by default to restrict Siri AI and other agents from capturing messages. The company says users can disable it in Signal's privacy settings, but doing so may expose their conversations to screen-reading assistants.
stories.detail: This is a new app-level response, not a claim that Signal's encryption has been broken. Signal says screenshot blocking is incomplete and does not stop every possible route to on-device data; the release is not described as Australia-restricted, but depends on the app and OS version.

stories.title: Italy provisionally approves Tesla's supervised driving system
stories.summary: Italy's transport minister announced provisional approval for Tesla Assisted Driving, following a technical assessment and ahead of wider EU approval. Tesla also confirmed the decision, expanding the system's European reach beyond the smaller countries that had already recognised it.
stories.detail: Despite the naming, this remains supervised driver assistance, not permission for unattended driving. The Italian decision does not change Australian approvals or confirm any new feature for your Model Y; local availability still depends on the vehicle, software, hardware and applicable requirements.

stories.title: ChatGPT Space starts rolling out to Plus subscribers
stories.summary: OpenAI says adults on Plus are gaining Space globally, including Australia, for creating and collaboratively editing interactive pages and presentations. Pages and slides can also be set to update using connected apps and tools, although rollout and access still depend on the account.
stories.detail: A possible use for you: keep an approved customer-review outline and action tracker together, then refine them as new meeting notes arrive. That is a suggested application, not a reported customer deployment; shared content requires permission and a supported paid account with Space access, and there are no public links.

stories.title: Trump threatens a tax on US firms building data centres abroad
stories.summary: Donald Trump says he wants to penalise American companies that build data centres overseas, in an effort to keep AI infrastructure in the US. The ABC notes that Microsoft and Amazon have already announced major Australian investments, making the threat relevant well beyond China.
stories.detail: There is no detailed tax proposal, implementation date or confirmed change to those Australian projects. The practical issue to watch is whether the rhetoric becomes an actual policy affecting overseas cloud capacity, rather than assuming announced local facilities have been cancelled.

stories.title: Reuters says the SEC's Nvidia inquiry is examining accounting
stories.summary: Two people briefed on the matter told Reuters that US securities investigators are scrutinising potential accounting issues at Nvidia. That identifies a focus not established in earlier reporting about the investigation, making it a substantive development rather than another stock-price update.
stories.detail: Reuters could not establish precisely which accounting issues are under review or when the inquiry began. The SEC declined to comment and Nvidia did not immediately respond; an investigation is not evidence of wrongdoing or a finding that its accounts are incorrect.

stories.title: Australia and China agree a new AI dialogue after Beijing talks
stories.summary: The new development after yesterday's Xi meeting is an agreement to hold government talks on AI, reached during Albanese's subsequent meeting with Premier Li Qiang in Beijing. The discussions are intended to share experience as both countries consider how the technology should be regulated.
stories.detail: This is a diplomatic dialogue, not a joint product launch or a change to Australian rules on using Chinese AI services. It comes alongside Australia's separate US technology-supply-chain commitments, illustrating its attempt to cooperate with China while managing security concerns.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill eight and hit Kyiv bridges and power infrastructure
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials reported eight deaths in a major Russian missile and drone attack on Friday, including six in Kyiv and two at a railway station in Lviv. Electricity, water and transport infrastructure were hit, with emergency outages introduced in several regions.
stories.detail: The attack follows the latest strikes on the bridge to occupied Crimea, but is a new escalation with fresh casualties and civilian-service disruption. Reuters said it could not independently verify all the accounts; both sides deny targeting civilians.

stories.title: Myanmar rejects genocide ruling and leaves refugee returns conditional
stories.summary: Myanmar's foreign ministry rejected the International Court of Justice's finding that the state committed genocide against the Rohingya, calling the judgment unfair. It said displaced people could return only when conditions permit, despite the court's requirement for safe returns and compensation.
stories.detail: The ruling itself was delivered on Thursday; Friday's rejection is the fresh development. The ICJ decides state responsibility rather than individual criminal guilt, and its limited enforcement powers leave implementation and the position of refugees unresolved.

afternoon.note: New developments since this morning. Times are Sydney local unless noted.

stories.title: Teenager charged after Castle Hill shopping centre stabbings
stories.summary: Police have charged a 17-year-old after two 16-year-old boys were stabbed at Castle Towers on Friday afternoon. One boy remains in a critical condition and the other is stable, police said today.
stories.detail: Police say the people involved had some prior knowledge of each other and are looking for another person. The teenager has been refused bail and is due to appear before a children's court on Sunday; the charges remain allegations.

stories.title: Families rally over homebirth insurance changes
stories.summary: Thousands of people rallied across Australia today against changes to insurance requirements for privately practising midwives. Advocates say the changes could reduce access to midwife-supported homebirths, particularly outside major cities.
stories.detail: An exemption allowing private midwives to attend homebirths without indemnity insurance ends on 1 January. Health Minister Mark Butler says practitioners should have insurance for births; advocates argue the available policy is not suitable or accessible for all midwives.

editions.label: Friday, 20 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates and availability limits are labelled.

stories.title: Labor names former Liberal councillor Tanya Raffoul for Epping
stories.summary: Parramatta councillor Tanya Raffoul has been named Labor's candidate for Epping after leaving the Liberals and joining Labor this week. The former adviser to Coalition minister David Elliott said she had grown apart from the party and was concerned about its relationship with One Nation.
stories.detail: This puts a familiar local-government figure into the contest for your state seat, currently held by Liberal Monica Tudehope. Labor approached Raffoul after she backed a Labor candidate for Parramatta lord mayor; this is a candidate announcement, not a change of MP.

stories.title: NSW political staff union threatens action over office security
stories.summary: The Public Service Association has lodged a workplace dispute after parliament's presiding officers declined its request for a joint security committee. Staff report threats, abuse and violence, with the issue receiving renewed attention after the alleged attack on federal MP Helen Haines.
stories.detail: A conciliation hearing is listed for today, so industrial action is a threat rather than an announced closure of electorate offices. Parliament says it is already reviewing security arrangements; the dispute concerns the safety of the staff who handle constituents' calls, emails and visits.

stories.title: Apple wins the right to discuss the UK's secret data-access order
stories.summary: The UK's Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the government's attempt to keep its demand for access to encrypted Apple customer data secret. Much of the challenge can now be heard publicly, rather than behind closed doors.
stories.detail: The important distinction is that this is a ruling about secrecy, not a final decision overturning the data-access demand or restoring Advanced Data Protection in the UK. No change to Australian iCloud settings or availability was announced, but the case remains an important test of government pressure on encryption.

stories.title: Tesla starts Cybercab rides in Dallas
stories.summary: Tesla's Robotaxi account announced that Cybercab rides have launched in Dallas, taking the steering-wheel-free two-seater beyond Austin. Not a Tesla App reports that the Dallas vehicles use the V1.5 design, with integrated Starlink equipment and a rear luggage-area camera spotted by riders.
stories.detail: This is a commercial-service expansion, not just a demonstration or factory promise. It is US-only news with no confirmed Australian launch, and does not make an Australian Model Y driverless or change the supervision requirements of any features already fitted to your car.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App, citing Tesla Robotaxi

stories.title: Musk floats shifting Model Y production to the larger Model Y L
stories.summary: At the DealBook Summit, Elon Musk suggested Tesla should consider switching Model Y production to its larger six-seat Model Y L, citing demand. Not a Tesla App reports that some US buyers are already facing longer waits for that model.
stories.detail: There is no confirmed production-conversion timetable or announcement that the standard Model Y is being discontinued worldwide. For Australian owners, this is a possible future line-up change to watch, not a recall, service-policy change or reason to expect anything different from your existing vehicle today.

stories.title: Gemini gains computer control on Mac, initially in the US
stories.summary: Google is rolling out a Mac feature that can click through apps, type into forms and work with local files in an isolated background window. Its examples include turning dashboard metrics and screenshots into Google Slides, with a live preview, app permissions and approval for key actions.
stories.detail: That is a reported use case with obvious potential for preparing a customer review, but the rollout is English-language and US-only, not confirmed for Australia. Put it on the watchlist rather than expecting to use it here now, and keep customer-data access within workplace-approved tools.

stories.title: Canva adds switches for generative tools and AI-made assets
stories.summary: Canva Free and Pro users can now hide generative AI features and reduce AI-generated templates and elements in library results, at no extra charge. Background Remover and Magic Grab remain available because they edit existing material rather than generate new content.
stories.detail: For a presentation, try the reduced-AI-content setting when you want more human-made visual assets; that is a suggested application, not a reported customer example. Canva lists no Australian exclusion, while managed workplace accounts continue to have separate administrator controls.

stories.title: Anthropic makes its Nasdaq debut after a roughly US$81 billion offering
stories.summary: The maker of Claude began trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, becoming the first publicly traded frontier AI company, Reuters reports. The scale of the offering puts funding for expensive computing infrastructure, and the path to profitability, under public-market scrutiny.
stories.detail: This is a major industry financing milestone, not a new Claude model or a change to subscriptions. Anthropic says the offering is expected to close on 20 November, subject to the usual conditions.
stories.source: Reuters; offering details checked with Anthropic

stories.title: Three-way summit ends with a broad statement, but no Ukraine deal
stories.summary: Trump, Xi and Putin concluded their Shenzhen talks with a declaration on nuclear risks, energy supplies and possible UN reform. The official account did not mention Ukraine, despite Trump saying beforehand that the war would be discussed.
stories.detail: The leaders backed more refined-fuel production and supply without numerical targets or a timetable, so this is not an agreed fix for energy-market disruption. Before the meeting, Anthony Albanese directly called on Putin to end the invasion; no ceasefire or peace settlement emerged from the published readout.

stories.title: Revised COP31 draft drops fossil fuel language
stories.summary: Negotiators removed references to ending fossil fuel use from the latest draft, along with a US$120 billion adaptation-finance target, Reuters reports. Australia and Türkiye defended the narrowing of the text as the talks approached Friday's deadline.
stories.detail: This is a substantive retreat from the earlier draft, but not yet the final agreement. Fossil fuel commitments and funding for vulnerable countries remain the issues to watch as negotiations continue.

afternoon.note: New developments since this morning. Times are Sydney local unless noted.

stories.title: Man charged after counter-terror raids across Sydney
stories.summary: A 35-year-old man has been charged with terrorism offences after police searched properties across Sydney this morning. The AFP alleges he researched a vehicle-borne explosive device and possessed violent extremist material.
stories.detail: Police say they have no information suggesting a target was identified or that he had the capability to carry out an attack, and say there is no ongoing threat to the community. The allegations are yet to be tested in court.

stories.title: Former NSW MP Daryl Maguire jailed over visa conspiracy
stories.summary: Former Wagga Wagga MP Daryl Maguire has been sentenced to three years in prison, with a one-year non-parole period, for his role in a fraudulent visa scheme. A jury found him guilty of conspiracy in July.
stories.detail: His lawyers indicated they would appeal the conviction and sought bail, which was refused. The court heard the scheme involved false or misleading visa applications while Maguire was a sitting MP.

stories.title: Albanese and Xi meet as Australian businesses seek trade access
stories.summary: Anthony Albanese met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen today, with Xi describing a turnaround in Australia-China relations and Albanese calling for frank discussions despite differences. It was their fifth meeting since Albanese became prime minister.
stories.detail: Australian businesses are pressing for greater access to Chinese markets, including beef and rice, as the prime minister heads to Beijing for further meetings. No change to beef quotas was announced in the reporting on the Xi meeting.

editions.label: Thursday, 19 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Announcements and unreleased features are labelled.

stories.title: Macquarie Park project backs a push for more factory-built homes
stories.summary: A new Committee for Sydney report calls for a steady pipeline of government housing projects to support investment in prefabrication factories. A nearby example is Macquarie Park student accommodation, where 19 storeys of modular rooms were assembled in 19 weeks.
stories.detail: Its developer says the overall project will be about 25% quicker than conventional construction. The report argues faster, more predictable building could help increase housing supply, but this is a policy proposal, not a newly funded construction programme.

stories.title: Domain forecasts more Sydney price falls before a recovery
stories.summary: Domain's new forecast expects Sydney house prices to fall by 10% by June 2027, then stabilise in the second half of the year. It also predicts Sydney will lead the eventual recovery among capital cities, rather than bounce back immediately.
stories.detail: The ABC reports that high borrowing costs and weak buyer confidence are weighing on demand. Treat this as one firm's outlook, not a valuation of an individual property: the timing of a turn, and conditions in specific suburbs, remain uncertain.

stories.title: Sydney councils move against smart glasses at pools and beaches
stories.summary: Inner West Council has banned smart glasses at its swimming and recreation facilities, while Waverley has approved a beach ban in principle and is consulting on enforcement. Randwick and Northern Beaches councils are also examining beach restrictions over privacy and covert-filming concerns.
stories.detail: Premier Chris Minns says he will consider statewide action. These are different local decisions at different stages, not a blanket NSW ban already in force, so check the rules of the facility you visit.

stories.title: Apple's Creator Studio updates arrive, including new Keynote tools
stories.summary: The previously announced updates are now rolling out, with MotionVFX tools in Final Cut Pro, Generate Fill in Pixelmator Pro and intelligent assistants in Keynote, Pages and Numbers. Existing Creator Studio subscribers receive the updates without an additional subscription charge.
stories.detail: For presentation work, the important caveat is that the assistants are beta features, require an Apple Intelligence-capable device on version 27 or later, and support US English only. Australian-language support is not confirmed; check those requirements before expecting them on your Mac.

stories.title: Tesla's iPhone app switches its maps to Google
stories.summary: Not a Tesla App reports that version 4.63.0 replaces Apple Maps tiles and satellite imagery with Google's. Its testing found smoother zooming into Supercharger Site Maps, which previously required a switch between the two map providers.
stories.detail: This is a phone-app change, not a Model Y firmware update or new driving capability. It could make checking your car's location and charging stops smoother, but an Australian rollout date and availability at individual local charging sites were not separately confirmed.

stories.title: App code hints at manual battery preconditioning
stories.summary: Not a Tesla App found references to start and stop battery-preconditioning buttons in the new app. The text suggests drivers could warm the battery themselves before DC fast charging, rather than relying solely on navigation to a supported charger.
stories.detail: Tesla has not announced or enabled the feature, and supported vehicles and Australian availability are unknown. It could eventually help Model Y owners prepare for a nearby fast charger, but it is not a button you should expect to find today, nor a benefit for ordinary AC charging.

stories.title: ChatGPT dictation now streams text and loses its 10-minute limit
stories.summary: OpenAI says Live Dictation displays your words as you speak, rather than making you wait for transcription at the end. It is rolling out globally to all plans on iPhone, Android, the web and desktop, so Australia is included in that rollout.
stories.detail: Try this: dictate a short, non-sensitive post-call recap, then ask for decisions, action owners and a follow-up draft. That is a suggested workflow, not a reported customer example; review names and commitments before sharing, and do not treat dictation as automatic meeting recording.

stories.title: Reuters investigation raises privacy concerns about Meta's Muse agent
stories.summary: Reuters reviewed internal reports of Muse taking unwanted actions and tested access to Signal messages through device permissions. Meta called the examples isolated incidents and said many apparent account mix-ups were fabricated answers already addressed, not confirmed data leaks.
stories.detail: Reuters could not establish whether apparently unrelated financial details were real or invented. The practical takeaway for experimenting with agents: review notification, screen and accessibility access, and keep purchases and outbound messages behind approval rather than assuming an unconnected app is inaccessible.

stories.title: New report puts Australia's data centre energy demand under scrutiny
stories.summary: The Climate Council warns that nine large proposed data centres could substantially increase emissions if powered mainly by fossil fuels. It wants mandatory standards requiring developers to bring on additional renewable electricity and storage, rather than simply add demand to the existing grid.
stories.detail: The industry disputes the report's assumptions and says developers already offset much of their demand with renewables. National rules are expected in the coming months; the key distinction is between projected demand from proposed projects and electricity being consumed today.

stories.title: Trump arrives in China ahead of three-way talks with Xi and Putin
stories.summary: Xi Jinping personally greeted Donald Trump at Shenzhen airport before the leaders' planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of APEC. A US official also told Reuters that separate Trump-Putin talks are planned.
stories.detail: Ukraine, strategic stability and the wider relationship between the powers are in focus, but no agreement from the trilateral meeting has been announced. Anthony Albanese says any peace in Ukraine must be on Ukraine's terms, and is due to meet Xi on Friday.

stories.title: Democrats nominate Jeffries for US House speaker
stories.summary: House Democrats elected Hakeem Jeffries their leader following their midterm victory, positioning him to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress convenes in January. US media reported a 251-11 vote in his favour.
stories.detail: This is the party nomination, not the final House vote installing a speaker. A Democratic majority would give the party greater control over legislation and investigations during Trump's final two years, while Jeffries also faces pressure from progressives over how to use that power.

afternoon.note: New developments since this morning. Times are Sydney local unless noted.

stories.title: Coroner finds Silverwater death in custody was preventable
stories.summary: NSW State Coroner Teresa O'Sullivan has found that the 2022 death of Aboriginal woman Tammy Shipley at Silverwater Women's Correctional Centre was preventable. She identified failures by police and Corrective Services in the lead-up to the death.
stories.detail: The coroner made 10 recommendations aimed at improving systems across NSW Police, Corrective Services and Justice Health. Shipley, a mother of five, died after drinking excessive water associated with a psychiatric condition.

stories.title: Unemployment rises to 4.9% as employment falls
stories.summary: Australia's unemployment rate rose to 4.9% in October, its highest since October 2021, according to figures released by the ABS today. Seasonally adjusted employment fell by 43,500 and the number of unemployed people rose by 17,800.
stories.detail: The trend unemployment rate rose to 4.8%, suggesting the softer labour market is not just a single monthly swing. Economists cited by the ABC expect the Reserve Bank to hold rates in the near term, but that is a forecast, not a decision.
